title: Not believing in the Hereafter, they named angels female.
subtitle: Careless claims grow where accountability is denied
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah admonishes the idolaters for {trap}calling the angels by female names and claiming they were Allah's daughters{/trap}. He cites another verse: did they witness their creation? {idea}Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.{/idea}
now: When you think no one will ever check, you say things more loosely. A review you never verified. A claim about someone at work. {idea}Belief in a Day of questions makes your words careful.{/idea}
old: What I say about things I cannot see does not really matter.
new: Every claim I make will be recorded and asked about.
try: Before you state something as fact today, ask yourself: could I answer for this?

title: Guessing never takes the place of truth.
subtitle: No knowledge, only assumption
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}conjecture is of no benefit and never takes the place of truth{/trap}. He quotes the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most lying speech.{/idea}
now: Your colleague did not reply to your message, and in your head a whole story builds: they are angry, they dislike you, they are plotting. {trap}It is all a guess.{/trap} A guess, however detailed, is still not the truth.
old: I am pretty sure, so it is basically true.
new: A guess, however confident, is worth nothing against the truth.
try: Catch one assumption you make about someone today and ask them instead.

title: Turn from the one who wants only this world.
subtitle: When someone has turned their back on the Reminder
then: The Prophet ﷺ was told to {idea}withdraw from the one who turns away from the Reminder{/idea}. Ibn Kathir describes such a person as one {trap}whose aim and knowledge are concentrated on this life{/trap} alone.
now: You spend hours in comment threads arguing with someone who has no interest in listening. Your evening is gone, your heart is heavier. {idea}Some conversations are a signal to step back.{/idea}
old: I must win every argument about faith.
new: When someone has turned away, I can step back and guard my own heart.
try: Leave one pointless argument today, online or off, without a last word.

title: That is as far as their knowledge reaches.
subtitle: When this world is the whole syllabus
then: Ibn Kathir says seeking this life was {trap}the best knowledge they had acquired{/trap}. He mentions the supplication: {idea}O Allah, do not make this world our greatest concern, nor the limit of our knowledge.{/idea}
now: You know your phone plan, the best exchange rate, the price of every car you might buy. {trap}Can you say as much about what comes after?{/trap} The verse names a ceiling many of us live under.
old: Being well informed about this world is enough.
new: If this world is all I know, my knowledge has stopped too early.
try: Say the dua today: O Allah, do not make this world my greatest concern.

title: Everything is His, so every deed is answered.
subtitle: Ownership leads to recompense
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}created the creation in truth{/idea} and rules it with justice. He repays each by their deeds. Notice the difference: evil is met with what it did, but good is met with {reward}what is best{/reward}.
now: You helped your neighbor carry boxes and nobody thanked you. You snapped at your child and nobody saw. {idea}Nothing in the world is ownerless, so nothing is lost.{/idea} And the good is repaid with more than it was.
old: Most of what I do goes unnoticed and unanswered.
new: Allah owns everything, so every deed is answered, and good with the best.
try: Do one good deed today that nobody will see.

title: Vast forgiveness, so do not praise yourselves.
subtitle: Avoid the big sins, and stay humble
then: Ibn Kathir says the good-doers avoid major sins, and their {reward}minor faults are forgiven{/reward}. He knew you in the womb. The Prophet ﷺ changed a girl's name from Barrah, the pious one, saying {idea}do not claim purity for yourselves{/idea}.
now: Your profile says blessed and grateful. In your head you rank yourself against the cousin who stopped praying. {trap}Self-praise is quiet and easy.{/trap} The verse reminds you who knew you before your mother did.
old: Compared to others, I am doing pretty well.
new: He knew me in the womb. Only He knows who is truly good.
try: When you feel better than someone today, stop and ask Allah to forgive you both.

title: Have you seen the one who turned away?
subtitle: A portrait that begins with turning
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah here {trap}chastises those who turn away from His obedience{/trap}. He links it to another verse: he neither believed nor prayed, but denied and turned away. The next verses fill in the portrait.
now: You used to read Quran after Fajr. Then once a week. Then the app sits unopened on your phone. {trap}Turning away rarely feels like a decision.{/trap} The verse asks you to look at the person who turned, and check your own direction.
old: Turning away is something other people do, dramatically.
new: Turning away can happen quietly, and I should check my direction.
try: Pick up one good habit you let slip, and do it once today.

title: He gave a little, then stopped.
subtitle: Like diggers who hit a rock and quit
then: Ibn Abbas said: {trap}gave a little, then stopped giving{/trap}. Ikrimah and Sa'id gave a picture: people digging a well hit a rock, say {trap}we are finished{/trap}, and abandon the work.
now: You set up a monthly donation, then cancel it the first tight month. You started visiting your aunt, then stopped after one awkward visit. {idea}The first rock is where giving is tested.{/idea}
old: I gave once. That counts, even if I stopped.
new: The test is not the first gift, but carrying on past the first rock.
try: Restart one small act of giving you dropped, even at a smaller amount.

title: Does he see the unseen, that he fears poverty?
subtitle: Stinginess pretends to know the future
then: Ibn Kathir says he stopped giving {trap}for fear of poverty{/trap}, as if he knew the future. The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}Spend, Bilal, and do not fear less provision from the Owner of the Throne.{/reward}
now: Payday comes, you see a request for help, and the thought arrives: what if I need this later? {trap}That thought acts as if it can see next month.{/trap} It cannot. The Provider can.
old: If I give now, I might not have enough later.
new: I cannot see the future, but I know Who replaces what I spend.
try: Give a small amount today before the what-if thought finishes.

title: Has he not heard what Musa's scriptures said?
subtitle: An old message, already delivered
then: The surah asks whether this man was never told {idea}what is in the scriptures of Musa{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says the verses that follow are what Allah revealed in the scriptures of Ibrahim and Musa. The message was not new.
now: You hear a hard truth about responsibility and want to wave it away as someone's opinion. {idea}Some truths have been repeated by every prophet.{/idea} When something is that old and that consistent, it deserves a pause.
old: This is just one more opinion I can ignore.
new: This truth was already in Musa's scriptures. It is not new.
try: Read the next few verses slowly, as words told to many prophets before.

title: And Ibrahim, who fulfilled everything.
subtitle: One word that sums up a life
then: Ibn Abbas said {idea}he delivered all that Allah ordered him to deliver{/idea}. Qatadah said he obeyed Allah and conveyed His message. Ibn Kathir links it to the trials Ibrahim completed, after which Allah made him {reward}a leader for mankind{/reward}.
now: You finish nine steps of a task and leave the last annoying one for later. Most people do. {idea}Ibrahim is remembered with one word: he finished.{/idea}
old: Doing most of what is asked is good enough.
new: Ibrahim is honored because he fulfilled all of it.
try: Finish one task today that you left at ninety percent.

title: No one carries another's load.
subtitle: Each soul carries its own
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}every soul shall carry its own wrongs{/idea}, and no one else will carry them. He cites another verse: if one heavily laden calls another to help, {trap}nothing will be lifted, even by a close relative{/trap}.
now: You grew up blamed for your brother's mistakes, or you lean on your parents' piety to cover your own gaps. {idea}Neither is how the scales work.{/idea} You are not carrying their load, and they are not carrying yours.
old: I will be judged with my family, or because of them.
new: I carry only my own load, and no one can carry it for me.
try: Let go of guilt for one thing that was someone else's choice, not yours.

title: You have only what you strive for.
subtitle: Effort is the currency
then: Ibn Kathir says the soul {idea}only benefits from the good it earns for itself{/idea}. Even the three things that continue after death in the hadith, {reward}a righteous child, ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge{/reward}, are in reality the results of one's own efforts.
now: You are raising kids, teaching a younger colleague, planting a tree outside the building. {reward}Those efforts keep counting after you stop.{/reward} What you build now is what you will have.
old: What I get in the end is mostly luck or other people.
new: What I get is what I strove for, including what keeps going after me.
try: Teach someone one useful thing today.

title: Your effort will be seen.
subtitle: Nothing done is invisible

row.title: it will be shown
sub: by the Knower of the unseen

then: Ibn Kathir says this means {idea}on the Day of Resurrection{/idea}, citing: Do deeds, Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger and the believers. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, {reward}who will tell you what you used to do{/reward}.
now: You stayed late to fix a mistake that was not yours. You cared for a parent for years and nobody at work knew. {reward}It will be seen.{/reward} Nothing done for Allah is invisible.
old: If no one sees my effort, it is wasted.
new: Every effort will be seen, even the ones no one noticed.
try: Do one hidden kindness today and keep it between you and Allah.

title: Then it is repaid in full.
subtitle: The fullest recompense
then: The sequence ends here. The effort is made, it is seen, and {reward}then it is repaid with the fullest recompense{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says Allah repays in the best manner, good for good and evil for evil.
now: Your payslip never matches the hours you really put in. Your parents never got repaid for what they gave you. {reward}This verse promises a payment that is complete.{/reward}
old: Life never pays me back for what I give.
new: Nothing is underpaid with Allah. It comes back in full.
try: Think of one effort that felt unrewarded and hand it over to Allah in a short dua.
